purpose: Fluorometholone is a steroid eye drop used to reduce redness, swelling, and irritation in your eyes caused by inflammation. It is commonly prescribed after eye surgery or for certain eye conditions like allergic reactions or inflammatory eye diseases. It helps your eyes heal and feel more comfortable.
how_it_works: Fluorometholone works by calming down your immune system's response in your eye. When your eye is irritated or inflamed, your body releases chemicals that cause swelling and redness. This medication blocks those chemicals, reducing inflammation and helping your eye feel better.
common_side_effects: You may notice mild stinging or burning right after putting in the drops. Some people experience temporary blurred vision, increased sensitivity to light, or a feeling that something is in their eye. These effects are usually mild and short-lived.
warnings: Do not use these drops if you have a viral, fungal, or bacterial eye infection unless your doctor specifically says so, as steroids can make infections worse. Long-term use can raise the pressure inside your eye (glaucoma) or cause cataracts, so regular eye check-ups are important. Do not stop using this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye 2 to 4 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. Always shake the bottle well before use and wash your hands before putting in the drops. Do not touch the tip of the dropper to your eye or any surface to keep it clean.
